transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay, Elena, Tom, Priya (Redwood); Marcus, Kira, Diego, Hannah (Aperture Node)

Summary (auto): Quick ops handoff to Aperture Node SREs covering marketplace packaging, KMS integration, and UAT plan. Agreed action items: send packaging checklist, share KMS matrix, schedule UAT.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Sanjay Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — this is the handoff for the Connector packaging and marketplace listing work.
[00:00:09] Marcus Lee: Hey all, Marcus here. We've got Kira and Diego from platform. Hannah's on for product questions.
[00:00:14] Elena Ruiz: Elena from Redwood, I'll be doing the deep sysops walkthrough.
[00:00:18] Tom Nguyen: Tom, solutions eng, and I'll cover the UAT runbook bits.
[00:00:23] Kira Osei: Kira, Platform Engineer. We set aside an internal cluster for testing.
[00:00:27] Diego Ramos: Diego, SRE — curious about networking and KMS details mostly.
[00:00:31] Sanjay Patel: Great, goal for today: make sure your infra team can install the connector in both marketplace (cloud list) mode and in private V-P-C / on-prem flow, confirm any blockers, and align on next steps.
[00:00:48] Hannah Cole: Sounds good. Also want to know what the required security artifacts are for marketplace listing — like audit logs, SOC two, SSO.
[00:00:57] Elena Ruiz: Yeah, we have a listing checklist. We'll share it but quick callouts: SSO/SAML metadata, RBAC matrix, audit logging endpoints, and K-M-S details. Some of the field names in the marketplace manifest are a bit picky.
[00:01:10] Marcus Lee: When you say K-M-S details, do you support external KMS or only cloud KMS? That matters for our compliance.
[00:01:18] Tom Nguyen: We support external KMS via our connector with HSM integration; it's in the compatibility matrix. There are knobs for key rotation and envelope encryption. We'll send the doc.
[00:01:29] Diego Ramos: Any latency or crypto overhead we should expect with H-S-M backing?
[00:01:33] Elena Ruiz: Minimal for unwrap/wrap, depends on how often you call the KMS; we recommend caching decrypted keys for the lifetime of the node process and using rotation windows. Also watch for concurrency on key unwraps during scale events.
[00:01:48] Kira Osei: On networking: what's the recommended egress pattern for private deployment? We need to limit outbound to only specific Redwood endpoints.
[00:01:56] Sanjay Patel: Use the VPC egress allowlist we provide. For private deployments the connector only needs outbound to api.redwood-inference.com and the telemetry endpoint. We'll provide IP ranges in the checklist.
[00:02:08] Marcus Lee: Are those ranges stable? Our infra team wants long-lived CIDR blocks for firewall rules.
[00:02:12] Elena Ruiz: We publish region-specific CIDR blocks, but for private deployments we also support a static egress NAT pool when customers run the connector in their VPC. We'll note that in the packaging doc.
[00:02:25] Hannah Cole: Marketplace listing — what about the billing metering integration? Do we need to embed metering hooks?
[00:02:32] Tom Nguyen: For marketplace listings we expose a usage endpoint that the marketplace can poll. We can also emit metering events to your marketplace account. There's a small shimming step in the chart values.
[00:02:44] Diego Ramos: Any changes required to our helm charts? We're already running a custom operator.
[00:02:48] Elena Ruiz: We provide a Helm subchart and an operator bundle. If you have a custom operator, you can either wrap our subchart or install side-by-side; the main requirement is to ensure CRDs are applied in the right order and the service account has the correct RBAC. We had one customer call the CRD ordering the "C-R-D tango" which is, uh, true.
[00:03:06] Kira Osei: Ha, the C-R-D tango. Noted.
[00:03:10] Marcus Lee: Walk us through the on-prem flow — we need air-gapped compatibility for a subset of customers.
[00:03:16] Elena Ruiz: For air-gapped installs the pattern is: bundle the OCI images into a tarball, provide an offline package with the operator and helm chart, and supply a small bootstrap script. We also provide a local K-V cache configuration — excuse me, the KV cache settings — to avoid outbound calls.
[00:03:30] Sanjay Patel: Important callout: some of our attention optimizations expect kernel-level ops; in air-gapped mode you'll want to pin to the quantized runtime we ship for on-prem so you don't hit a mismatched lib. We'll put explicit version pins.
[00:03:45] Diego Ramos: That kernel bit — can you clarify? We're running enterprise distros and worry about glibc/ABI differences.
[00:03:50] Elena Ruiz: Fair. We ship specific build artifacts for the quantized runtime and list the supported distro matrix (Ubuntu 20.04/22.04, RHEL 8.6+, etc.). If you have a different libc we can provide a statically-linked binary as a fallback, but that's heavier.
[00:04:06] Hannah Cole: From Product side, do you require us to display Redwood badges or logos in the UI for listing?
[00:04:11] Sanjay Patel: We request a small Redwood attribution in the listing metadata but branding guidelines are flexible; we'll send the guidelines.
[00:04:18] Marcus Lee: Can we talk about rollout and canaries? Our ops wants a canary process so we can validate each release in staging before prod.
[00:04:25] Tom Nguyen: We support canary rollouts via the operator — you can set a rollout percentage and route X% of traffic to the new version. For hosted API fallback, we have an automatic fallback policy if the connector fails to meet latency SLOs.
[00:04:40] Kira Osei: That fallback — does it send full requests to the hosted endpoints or masked ones? Concern about data exfil.
[00:04:46] Elena Ruiz: Good question. For private customers with strict residency, we can disable automatic hosted fallback; fallback is opt-in. If enabled, it's a configurable synchronous fallback to a tenant-scoped hosted instance; customers concerned about PII generally keep it off.
[00:05:03] Diego Ramos: Cool. About logs and audit trails — we need immutable audit logs and an S3-compatible sink. Do you emit structured audit events?
[00:05:11] Elena Ruiz: Yes, structured JSON events with request IDs, token anonymized fields, and a hash of the payload. We can forward to S3-compatible endpoints or to your SIEM via Kafka. We'll include a sample sink config in the repo.
[00:05:25] Hannah Cole: How about the marketplace acceptance criteria — like security scan results?
[00:05:29] Sanjay Patel: Marketplace teams typically want SBOM, SCA scan results, and our SOC two attestation. For some clouds they also need vulnerability scan reports for the images.
[00:05:39] Marcus Lee: We have a procurement note: if there are listing fees or metering differences, point us to the billing person.
[00:05:45] Tom Nguyen: I'll include the contact and a short rubric for metering integration, plus the small shim code snippet.
[00:05:51] (brief crosstalk)
[00:05:55] Kira Osei: On the technical side, we want to validate KV cache warmup — is there a recommended pattern to prefill caches during deploy?
[00:06:01] Elena Ruiz: Yes. We expose a prewarm endpoint you can call as a post-install hook. It accepts a list of prefixes to seed into the KV cache. For dynamic workloads, we recommend a warmup window to run after canary rollout.
[00:06:14] Diego Ramos: Any tips for load testing?
[00:06:16] Tom Nguyen: Use the lightweight harness (we'll share) and run a sequence of shorter and longer seq lengths — for example, 64-token and 1024-token runs — to capture attention scaling. Also test the continuous-batching path.
[00:06:30] Marcus Lee: Good — we'll run a perf test in our staging cluster.
[00:06:34] Hannah Cole: Question: are there infra-level probes we should wire for SLOs?
[00:06:38] Elena Ruiz: Yes: request latency p95/p99, token throughput, kv cache hit rate, and GPU memory pressure. We'll include Grafana dashboards you can import.
[00:06:50] Kira Osei: On RBAC — who owns the service account? Do we create one or should Redwood create and bind?
[00:06:56] Sanjay Patel: Customers create the service account in their cluster; we provide the exact role and rolebinding yaml. For marketplace installs the cloud marketplace will create a managed identity and the chart maps it to the service account.
[00:07:10] Diego Ramos: Anything about secret management we need to do?
[00:07:13] Elena Ruiz: We support external secret managers (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager). If you're using Vault, we have a mutating webhook example to inject credentials at runtime.
[00:07:23] Marcus Lee: Do you have a sample SAML metadata file for the marketplace SSO?
[00:07:27] Tom Nguyen: Yes in the repo under docs/sso. We'll reference it in the checklist.
[00:07:32] Kira Osei: One of our legal people asked about data retention for logs — is there a configurable retention on the telemetry pipeline?
[00:07:37] Elena Ruiz: Yep, retention is configurable per-tenant; default is 90 days but can be shortened. For enterprise you can set zero retention in hosted pipeline and route logs to your own S3.
[00:07:47] Hannah Cole: Are there pre-approved templates for the marketplace listing copy, icons, and screenshots?
[00:07:51] Sanjay Patel: We have templates. We'll send them in the checklist along with example screenshots and the required icon sizes.
[00:07:58] Marcus Lee: Great. Let's talk timeline: we want the connector listed and available as a preview in the marketplace by mid-August. Is that feasible?
[00:08:06] Sanjay Patel: If we get the checklist and test cluster provisioned this week and you run UAT the first week of August, mid-August listing is realistic. We need security artifacts and images signed by the 8th of August for marketplace gating.
[00:08:19] Marcus Lee: Okay we'll aim for that.
[00:08:22] Elena Ruiz: Quick note on image signing: we use cosign for signing artifacts; we'll provide the signing key guidance.
[00:08:29] Diego Ramos: One more thing — monitoring stack integration : do you have a Prometheus exporter?
[00:08:33] Tom Nguyen: Yes, exporter plus Grafana dashboards. Exporter exposes tokenized metrics and we can give a sample scrape config.
[00:08:41] Kira Osei: On the SRE side, Diego will run the first UAT.
[00:08:45] Diego Ramos: Yep, I'll take point, will need the runbook and the smoke script.
[00:08:49] Tom Nguyen: I'll put together the runbook and share a PR to your repo with the helper script.
[00:08:54] Marcus Lee: Any blockers we foresee that would delay mid-August?
[00:08:57] Elena Ruiz: Biggest potential blockers: image signing delay, unresolved KMS compatibility for a specific H-S-M vendor, or if the cluster can't allow the egress NAT we recommended.
[00:09:09] Hannah Cole: We'll prioritize the image signing and KMS checks.
[00:09:12] Sanjay Patel: Cool. Final recap: Redwood to share checklist, KMS matrix, samples for helm/operator, and the UAT runbook. Aperture Node to provision test cluster, confirm procurement contact, and run the UAT.
[00:09:27] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Let's capture the action items — Marcus will follow up internally and we'll sync next week.
[00:09:34] Elena Ruiz: I'll share a link to the doc — note, it's in PR form in our repo: https://redwood-inference.example.com/repos/aperturenode-connector/packaging-checklist (link), and the UAT harness is here: https://files.redwood-inference.example.com/harness/aperturenode-uatharness-v0.1.tar.gz
[00:09:52] Tom Nguyen: I'll schedule the kickoff for the UAT on Aug 2 and invite the SREs.
[00:09:58] Diego Ramos: Thanks everyone.
[00:10:00] Sanjay Patel: Thanks all — end of call.

--- End transcript ---

References shared: packaging checklist (link above), KMS matrix (to be shared), UAT harness tarball, sample helm values (will be posted to the repo).
